alt: Dark volcanic ridges and rock towers of the Jbel Saghro range under open sky
caption: The Jbel Saghro, a volcanic range of dark ridges, rock towers and dry plateaus between the Dadès and Drâa valleys. Four days of walking through it with a guide and mules are the core of this trip.

alt: Wide view over the Saghro mountains in southern Morocco
caption: The open, almost treeless country of the Saghro seen from a ridge. Camps are pitched on the plateaus between small Aït Atta villages, with no road in sight on most days.

alt: Rocky Saghro landscape with a ridge line at N'Handour
caption: Rock outcrops in the Saghro near N'Handour, one of the high points the traverse passes. In March days are mild but nights at camp can fall below freezing.

alt: Mud-brick kasbahs of Nkob at the southern foot of the Jbel Saghro
caption: Nkob, a ksar village of earth architecture on the southern edge of the Saghro. It is the usual finishing point or start of the long Saghro treks and a place to eat with a local family.

alt: Sea arch carved into red cliffs on Legzira beach seen from a distance
caption: The red sandstone cliffs and sea arch of Legzira on the Atlantic coast near Sidi Ifni. The beach is only walkable around low tide, and it opens the trip on the ocean before the road climbs inland to the Anti-Atlas.

alt: Villages and palm and almond groves in the Ameln valley of the Anti-Atlas
caption: The Ameln valley beneath the Anti-Atlas, with terraced almond and argan groves around Amazigh villages. Almond blossom here is a February event, so a mid-March trip sees green terraces and late petals rather than peak bloom.

alt: Panorama of the long Jbel el Kest ridge above Tafraoute
caption: Jbel Lekst, the long pink-granite ridge that shelters Tafraoute and the Ameln valley. Day walks on its flanks give the Anti-Atlas section of the trip its high views.

alt: A balanced rock formation known as Napoleon's Hat in the granite landscape near Tafraoute
caption: Napoleon's Hat, one of the balanced granite blocks in the boulder-strewn country around Tafraoute. The granite field is on foot or by short drives, with a campsite in town for the two tent nights.

alt: Old fortified kasbah building at Taliouine below the Siroua massif
caption: The old kasbah at Taliouine, the saffron town of the Souss at the foot of the Jbel Siroua. It is the base for a day walk into the Siroua and for the saffron cooperatives.

commonsFile: File:Near Taliouine, saffron crocus growing area - Flickr - gailhampshire.jpg
alt: Fields of the saffron crocus growing area near Taliouine
caption: The saffron-growing basin near Taliouine. The crocus is picked in autumn, so in March a visit is to the cooperative and the fields rather than the harvest.

alt: The volcanic Siroua massif rising above the Anti-Atlas plateau
caption: The volcanic Siroua massif, the high isolated block between the Anti-Atlas and High Atlas. Snow can lie on its upper slopes in March, which is why the walk here is a flexible weather day.

alt: The winding Tizi n'Tichka mountain road through the High Atlas
caption: The Tizi n'Tichka road over the High Atlas, the way back to Marrakech and the flight home. It rises above 2,000 m and can be affected by snow and ice in March.
